answer: On a coastal sensor market, an agent's gale forecast earns a vote only when its instrument signs a fresh signal and posts a tamper-evident raw trace to a shared vault. Each sensor serial can support one forecast per window; auditors sample devices at random and slash the deposit for forged traces. A swarm of new account names gains no extra votes without buying, maintaining, and bonding distinct sensors. Stolen signing chips or colluding auditors can still fool the check, so serial revocation and independent field tests remain necessary.
